Changeling Wayfinder: Solid playable and near-universal glue: a changeling body that ramps and fixes, satisfying every typal payoff while keeping your draft open. The 53.6% GIH is quiet but the +1.0 IWD undersells it — this is a first-few-picks stabilizer that gets better as your tribe firms up, especially into BG Elves or Vivid.
Rooftop Percher: Solid playable changeling. A 55% GIH at a late 6.2 ALSA means it fills any tribal deck for free — every creature type, satisfies typal payoffs, counts for Vivid pips, and keeps you open early in the draft. Take it as a cog, not a bomb.
Adept Watershaper: Premium early pick — first-pick-quality rare. 57.9% GIH with a 2.1 ALSA and 88% play rate means it goes in every deck and wins; the flat OH/GD split says it's good on turn one and late. A UW Merfolk payoff that never wants to wheel.
Ajani, Outland Chaperone: First-pick bomb. 60.9% GIH, +8.7 IWD, 1.5 ALSA and 86.8% play — the whole table takes it P1 and jams it. A white planeswalker that stabilizes and grinds; slam it, then build the rest of the deck around whatever it wants. No wheel, ever.
Appeal to Eirdu: Filler combat trick. 50% GIH WR, negative IWD, and a 7.7 ALSA all say the same thing: a marginal instant that doesn't move games. In a slow, flash-dense format, playable-but-cuttable — the 13th-16th card in an aggressive GW/UW build, sideboard elsewhere.
Bark of Doran: Filler-to-sideboard equipment. A sub-50% GIH WR with negative iwd on an equip cost confirms it's a tempo sink that doesn't move a game — in a slow format you'd rather have a body. Only splash it in a go-wide WG Kithkin shell that wants to punch through, and even then it's near the bottom of your playables.
Brigid, Clachan's Heart: First-pick bomb. 60.9% GIH with a 2.2 ALSA and near-uniform OH/GD split means she wins from any zone in any deck, not just Kithkin — a repeatable pinger/reach package that dominates board stalls. Take her over commons every time; splashable if needed.
Burdened Stoneback: Filler body. 53% GIH with a flat -0.2 iwd and a 4.5 ALSA that reflects table-open colorlessness, not desire — this is a curve-filler that gets blanked in a format where two-drops die to toughness. Play it only when short on bodies; it hits the magic 5-toughness club but does nothing else.
Champion of the Clachan: Solid early pick, not a bomb. 55.7% GIH with a 2.8 ALSA and 73.8% play rate reads as a reliable Kithkin anchor (GW), but the modest +2.3 IWD says it's a body that wants a wide board, not a game-ender. First-pickable for WG, a fine rate two/three-drop elsewhere.
Clachan Festival: Solid GW Kithkin payoff, not a slam. 56.5% GIH with a modest +2.2 IWD and 3.8 ALSA tells you it wants the weenie board to already exist — it's an anthem/engine, not a stand-alone card. Fine early pick if you're committed to Kithkin, but remember WG finished last: don't over-invest.
Crib Swap: Sideboard-to-fringe removal. A 50.2% GIH WR and negative IWD confirm the classic Crib Swap trade-off: you exile anything but hand the opponent a 1/1 Shapeshifter, so the tempo is often a wash. The Shapeshifter body counts as a changeling for typal payoffs, but at three mana for a soft answer this is a late playable, not a slam.
Curious Colossus: First-pick bomb. 62.9% GIH with +11.3 IWD and a 1.8 ALSA — it's leaving packs turn one for a reason. A W giant that dominates any board and plays in every white deck; the 66.1% drawn WR means it closes games whenever it lands. Slam it.
Eirdu, Carrier of Dawn: Bomb. 61.1% GIH with a huge +9.6 IWD and 1.5 ALSA means it's a first-pick that wheels to nobody. Slam it, splash it if needed — an Elemental God that swings games on its own. Trust the numbers; this is a build-around-me white finisher.
Encumbered Reejerey: Premium UW Merfolk common-tier uncommon: 56.4% GIH with an aggressive 3.6 ALSA and 85% play rate means it wheels almost never and everyone runs it. A tap/tempo Merfolk Soldier that fuels convoke and flash — core cog for the A-tier tempo build.
Evershrike's Gift: Filler aura, sideboard-adjacent. The -0.5 IWD and 5.8 ALSA say it's not helping you win the games you draw it — a flat 53% because auras carry 2-for-1 risk. Only maindeck it as a cheap enabler if your deck actively wants the buff; otherwise pass.
Flock Impostor: Solid playable changeling. 55.2% GIH is fine but the +0.8 IWD tells the story — it's a flexible cog that counts for every tribe (Merfolk, Kithkin, Elves) and keeps you open, not a needle-mover on its own. Prioritize in any typal build; unexciting filler in a non-synergy deck.
Gallant Fowlknight: Solid role-player, not a slam. 54.2% GIH with a flat IWD and ~49% play rate marks a fine white common body that fills curve without generating advantage. Fine in UW Merfolk tempo or GW Kithkin; take it mid-pack, never over removal or a lord.
Goldmeadow Nomad: Below-average two-drop cog. 52.6% GIH but negative iwd flags exactly the doctrine trap — a small Kithkin body that gets blanked once the board fills, contributing only in a dense WG weenie curve. Playable filler in aggro, cuttable everywhere else; don't pick it early over anything with reach or synergy.
Keep Out: Filler combat trick/protection. 52.6% GIH with -0.6 IWD and a late 5.3 ALSA is the profile of a card that's fine but never wanted — you play it when short on 23rd-card slots, cut it when you have real cards. Not worth prioritizing.
Kinbinding: First-pick premium removal. 64.3% GIH, +12.2 iwd, and a 1.8 ALSA scream bomb-tier: a cheap, splashable answer that any white deck wants maindeck. Nearly 90% play rate confirms it. Take it over almost anything and hold it for lords and flash finishers per doctrine.
Kinsbaile Aspirant: Premium Kithkin uncommon. 58.1% GIH and a spicy 61.9% OH WR mean it's at its best deployed early to snowball the go-wide plan — exactly the GW curve-out card. The OH>GD split confirms it's a proactive aggro cog; take it high when in Kithkin, pass if the lane is contested.
Kinscaer Sentry: Premium — first-pickable white rare. 59% GIH, +5.6 IWD, and a 2.2 ALSA (people take it near-instantly) confirm a two-drop that actually carries games, rare for the blanked two-slot. High OH (61.2%) means it hits early and keeps hitting. Slam it, splash it, play it in any white deck.
Kithkeeper: Solid playable, best in GW Kithkin and go-wide W decks. The 56.7% GD_WR and +3.7 IWD show it earns its keep once the board fills out, while the mediocre 48.8% OH_WR flags it as a build-around cog, not a turn-two drop. Good filler that gets better with more Kithkin around it.
Liminal Hold: Premium white common removal — this is Luminal Hold, the format's top white removal (3W exile a nonland permanent with lifegain, no drawback). 55.8% GIH and 87.3% play rate are underselling it because GIH chronically underrates removal. Prioritize highly; it's a P1-P2 in any white deck.
Meanders Guide: Filler-to-role-player. 54.1% GIH but -0.3 IWD flags it as replacement-level — a Merfolk cog whose value comes from the UW tempo shell, not raw stats. Fine as a 20th-23rd card in UW Merfolk to enable convoke/tap synergies; a cut everywhere else.
Moonlit Lamenter: Solid playable. The Treefolk body's toughness helps it dodge blight-based removal, and +2.9 IWD shows it pulls its weight when drawn. A grindy-good role-player for GW/BW; not a first-pick but a reliable early wheel-back at 3.9 ALSA.
Morningtide's Light: Solid playable, not the bomb the mythic tag implies. The 49% OH vs 57% GD split is the tell: a sorcery that's dead early and shines once there are targets/board state to leverage. Fine mid-pick removal-ish value, but don't slam it P1 over real removal.
Personify: Solid white role-player. 55.0% GIH with a low 52.5% OH_WR is a classic reactive-card profile — better drawn (56.6% GD) than in the opener because you want to hold it up. A fine playable, not a premium pick; 59.9% play means it wheels sometimes.
Protective Response: Premium white uncommon — first-pickable protection/combat instant. 57.2% GIH, +2.8 IWD, and an 89% play rate at 3.3 ALSA mean it's near-universal: convoke makes it near-free, and it protects your lords and engines from the format's deal-4 removal. Take it high.
Pyrrhic Strike: Premium white removal — first-pick-worthy. 58.3% GIH, +4.1 iwd, and an 88.6% play rate at ALSA 3.2 mean the format universally trusts it, and remember GIH underrates removal. Efficient interaction that any white deck slams; take it over most creatures and hold it for lords and flash finishers.
Reluctant Dounguard: Marginal Kithkin two-drop, and the format punishes exactly this — a vanilla-ish 2/2 body gets blanked on turn two. 51.6% GIH with -1.5 IWD and 40% play rate confirms it's a filler cog only GW Kithkin wants for density. Late pick.
Rhys, the Evermore: Solid rare, not a slam. 52.7% GIH and a near-zero +0.3 iwd say the token engine wins grinds but doesn't swing games on the draw; the 2.6 ALSA is name-value hype. Best in GW Kithkin or BG Elves go-wide; a fine playable, not a build-around bomb.
Riverguard's Reflexes: Role-player combat trick, not a maindeck lock. 52.7% GIH with a -1.0 IWD and only 23.9% play rate is the classic 'fine when it works, dead card in multiples' trick. Sideboard-adjacent; run one in a tempo UW deck to blow out attacks, but don't prioritize it.
Shore Lurker: Filler UW Merfolk body. 53.7% GIH with a flat +0.2 IWD and 6.5 ALSA — it wheels because it's a replaceable synergy cog, not a card you want. Playable if you're deep in Merfolk tap/convoke, cuttable otherwise. Don't prioritize.
Slumbering Walker: First-pick-worthy rare. 59.4% GIH WR, +5.9 IWD, and an ALSA of 2.1 mean the table already knows — it wheels almost never. A cheap, high-impact white bomb with five relevant toughness territory; take it over almost anything and build around it.
Spiral into Solitude: Trap outside blight decks. +0.0 IWD is the tell — the aura only earns its keep when blight-one is genuine upside (BW Blight, RB Goblins). In a non-blight white deck it's a real cost stapled to removal; the 54.3% GIH averages the built-around games with the misfires. Take it only when you're the blight deck.
Sun-Dappled Celebrant: Filler. 52.9% GIH and 48.3% play rate mark it as a marginal Treefolk body that only makes the deck when curve-starved. Not a synergy engine, no evasion — the kind of vanilla-ish two/three that gets blanked in a slow format. Late-pick roster fodder, GW Kithkin adjacent at best.
Thoughtweft Imbuer: Best of the white uncommons here and a legit high pick: 58.3% GIH and a strong +4.2 IWD mean it actively swings games it appears in. A Kithkin Advisor that wants GW Kithkin density but performs above the tribe's C-tier reputation — snap it up.
Timid Shieldbearer: Role-player two-drop that actually holds up — 55% GIH with a flat OH/GD line and cheap toughness that blocks the format's blanked-out aggressors. No synergy engine, so it's a competent GW/UW curve cog, not a priority. Take it late to fill the two-slot.
Tributary Vaulter: Playable Merfolk common. 55.4% GIH but +0.1 IWD and 6.3 ALSA scream replaceable synergy filler — it wins games as a UW cog on curve, not by being drawn late. Fine in UW Merfolk, a body elsewhere; let it come around.
Wanderbrine Preacher: Solid UW cog. 55.6% GIH with a strong 56% opening-hand read says it pulls weight early, not just as a late-game synergy piece. A merfolk with real support for the tempo/convoke plan — a comfortable, high-playability common. Prioritize it in UW.
Wanderbrine Trapper: Excellent white common-tier uncommon; near auto-pick. 59.5% GIH with a strong 62.1% opening-hand WR and +4.2 iwd says it performs early AND stays relevant. A Merfolk Scout that shines in UW tempo but is good enough to main in any white deck. Draft it high.
Winnowing: Solid rare removal but not a slam. The telling split — 47.7% OH versus 56.0% GD — means it's dead in your opener and a blowout once boards develop, so it's a mid-game sweeper you'd rather draw than hold. Prioritize as a strong playable, not a first pick.
Aquitect's Defenses: Sideboard/situational aura. 53% GIH looks fine but the 21% play rate and 7.2 ALSA reveal a niche card the good decks skip. Auras invite two-for-ones; only run it in tap-synergy UW Merfolk where the ability matters. Otherwise leave it in the pool.
Blossombind: Solid pseudo-removal common, especially in Vivid. 55.1% GIH at 83.3% play rate says it pulls its weight broadly — a cheap tap/lock aura that neutralizes a threat. Numot flags it as a happy Vivid inclusion; treat it as a serviceable answer, not a premium exile, since it leaves the body on board.
Champions of the Shoal: Bomb-tier blue rare, the best card in this chunk. 62.4% GIH and a monster +9.9 IWD mean it swings games hard the turn it lands; 2.6 ALSA shows the table knows. First pick in any UW Merfolk seat and a strong reason to be in blue at all.
Disruptor of Currents: Premium bomb, kill-on-sight caliber. 61.2% GIH WR with a monster +8.4 IWD and 88% play rate — the best card in this chunk. A UW Merfolk payoff that overperforms in any blue deck; slam it P1P1 and never pass it.
Flitterwing Nuisance: Strong blue rare, take early. 62.4% OH_WR with a 2.4 ALSA says it's an aggressive tempo threat that's best in your opener — a flash/evasive faerie rogue that fits UB Fairies/Flash or UW Merfolk. The IWD of +8.0 confirms real impact; don't pass it.
Glamer Gifter: Premium blue uncommon. 56.6% GIH, +3.2 IWD, an ALSA of 4.0 that says it's contested — a flash Faerie that ambushes and generates tempo/value in the format's high-flash environment. Prime UW Merfolk and UB Fairies pickup; respect the flash line and don't slam into its open mana.
Glamermite: Role-player, not a maindeck lock — 33.9% play rate and a wheeling 6.6 ALSA say it's a niche UB Fairies/Flash tool. The 53.2% GIH is fine but comes from the built-around evasive-tempo deck; outside UB flash it's cuttable filler.
Glen Elendra Guardian: Premium — take it. 56.6% GIH, 2.4 ALSA, 86% play rate: a flash faerie wizard that plays perfectly into ECL's off-curve, hold-up-mana texture. Slots UB Flash and UW, ambushes attackers, and the +3.8 IWD confirms it swings games. High pick.
Glen Elendra's Answer: Premium blue mythic. 59.3% GIH, +6.2 IWD and a strong 61.5% GD_WR — a flexible flash answer that rewards holding up mana, exactly what this off-curve format wants. High pick; the sub-60 OH is just the reactive tax. Take over most creatures.
Gravelgill Scoundrel: Solid blue common for UW/UB. 55.8% GIH and 56.5% OH WR show it's an early-game contributor, not just a synergy body — evasive rogue that pressures and enables flash/tap lines. Good pickup in merfolk or fairies; middle-of-the-pack priority.
Harmonized Crescendo: Rare with a pedestrian body of stats — 53.2% GIH and a flat +0.1 iwd say it's a solid-but-unexciting instant, not a bomb. The 63.6% play rate at ALSA 3.9 shows people run it when in blue, but it doesn't swing games alone. Fine role-player; don't overdraft on the rarity symbol.
Illusion Spinners: Niche UB Fairies/Flash payoff. 51.2% GIH with a low 30% play rate and OH/GD gap (47.8/53.4) marks it as a synergy card that underperforms in your opener — a role-player for flash decks, filler elsewhere. Wheel it unless you're committed to fairies.
Kulrath Mystic: Role-player, not a maindeck lock. 53.9% GIH with +1.4 iwd is respectable but the 34.5% play rate marks it as a UR Elementals cog you play when the deck comes together. Fine body, unexciting; take real cards over it early.
Loch Mare: Bomb — first-pick, first-pick. 62.1% GIH, +9.3 IWD, 1.7 ALSA and 88.9% play rate is the full bomb signature: it's played everywhere and wins the games it's drawn. A blue mythic that ends games on its own. Take it over anything.
Lofty Dreams: Serviceable UW Merfolk aura, role-player not premium. 55.3% GIH but the gap between 51.7% OH and 57.6% GD flags an aura's usual risk — dead in your opener, a real tempo/evasion swing once you have a body worth enchanting. Good with the tap/flyer plan; never a high pick.
Mirrorform: Strong blue trick/finisher, near-bomb. 55.5% GIH WR but the tell is the 8.4-point OH-to-GD split (50.3% vs 58.7%) — it's a reactive instant you want to draw, not mulligan to. Flexible clone-at-instant-speed value that rewards holding mana in the format's flash war. High pick.
Noggle the Mind: Solid blue uncommon control aura, a tempo/removal-ish enchantment. 55.2% GIH with +2.4 IWD is a reliable role-player; the 76.4% play rate is lower than the truly premium uncommons. Good in UW Merfolk or any blue deck that wants to neutralize a body — a P3-ish pickup, not a bomb.
Oko, Lorwyn Liege: Bomb planeswalker. 56.4% GIH looks modest but +7.2 IWD and 1.8 ALSA confirm it's a first-pick that ends games via repeatable value. The GIH is dragged by fair blue decks — in practice it protects itself and grinds. Take it over almost anything; slam.
Omni-Changeling: Premium changeling and a near-auto-include (86.5% play, 3.6 ALSA). Every creature type on a solid body means it turns on lords, Vivid pips, and typal payoffs in any deck while keeping your colors open — the flexible glue every tribal build wants.
Pestered Wellguard: Solid UW Merfolk cog. 54.5% GIH at a 4.1 ALSA — a tempo body the tribe actively wants, flat OH/GD so it works on curve and late. Good playable, not a bomb; wheel-ish in other colors but a priority in Merfolk where tap/convoke synergies compound.
Rime Chill: Niche playable, borderline sideboard. 52.4% GIH and a weak 47.8% OH_WR flag a purely reactive card you never want in your opener; the 36% play rate says most drafters cut it. A fine hold-up trick when UW tempo needs it, otherwise filler.
Rimefire Torque: Trap rare — a genuine bomb-hater's disappointment. 40.1% GIH, -7.9 IWD, and a 4.3% play rate are damning: nobody wants it and it actively loses games. Leave it in the pack; it doesn't fit any archetype's plan.
Rimekin Recluse: Top-tier blue uncommon — grab it. 60.2% GIH, +6.6 iwd, 90% play rate at ALSA 3.1 is elite across the board, meaning it wins whether early or late. An Elemental Wizard that anchors UR but any blue deck wants it. High pick, essentially always maindecked.
Run Away Together: Sideboard-to-filler tempo bounce. 51.2% GIH looks fine but the 22.5% play rate and 7.2 ALSA are the real tell — it needs two creature targets to shine and mostly rots in hand. Only maindeck in a tempo UW shell short on interaction.
Shinestriker: Premium Vivid payoff. 58.5% GIH and +6.4 iwd with a 3.9 ALSA make this the Vivid deck's engine — the 60.9% drawn WR is inflated by the built-around shell, so it's a strong pick specifically for 2c Vivid, merely good elsewhere. Prioritize when in Vivid.
Silvergill Mentor: Premium Merfolk uncommon and a card-advantage engine — exactly what the format rewards. 60.1% GIH with +5.2 IWD means it grinds; the UW tempo deck (WU) wants it as an early play that keeps refueling. High pick whenever you're in blue.
Silvergill Peddler: Merfolk curve-filler cog. 55% GIH but a dead-flat +0.0 IWD and 6.6 ALSA say it does nothing on its own — it's a body that enables tap/convoke synergies. Fine 20th-25th card in UW, first cut anywhere else.
Spell Snare: Sideboard card. 48.7% GIH WR, ~zero IWD, and a 13.5% play rate say the format's grindy midrange doesn't want a narrow counter maindeck. Board it in against known bombs or combo pieces; otherwise leave it out.
Stratosoarer: Playable blue common flyer with a ceiling. The gap between 51.0% OH and 57.0% GD_WR plus a 6.1 ALSA and 52.9% play rate marks it as a mid-game evasive body you draw into, not an early slam. Fine filler for UR Elementals / UW Merfolk that want the air; last-pick-able elsewhere.
Summit Sentinel: Filler/role-player. 53.7% GIH but 51.7% play and 6.5 ALSA say it's a late-table Elemental body that fills a curve slot rather than driving a plan. Playable in UR Elementals for pip count and blockers, but nothing to prioritize — a 21st-card.
Sunderflock: Bomb — take it over almost anything. 64.1% GIH with a monstrous +13.0 IWD and 2.4 ALSA is elite-rare territory; this UR Elemental single-handedly wins the games it lands in. First-pick, splash if you must.
Swat Away: Playable tempo removal — a convoke-discounted tuck. 54.7% GIH undersells it because GIH chronically underrates removal; the 51.7% OH vs 56.5% GD says hold it, don't cast it dead early. Interaction is scarce, so take it over marginal creatures in any blue deck.
Sygg, Wanderwine Wisdom: Bomb rare, near-P1. 60.6% GIH, +8.8 IWD, 2.2 ALSA and 87.9% play — the UW Merfolk payoff that snowballs card advantage in a format where the resource war decides games. Slam it and commit to UW tempo; it barely wheels.
Tanufel Rimespeaker: Strong UR uncommon. 56.3% GIH, +3.8 IWD, and 83% play at 4.0 ALSA mark a real elemental payoff/value wizard that earns its slot. Prioritize in UR Elementals where its type and ability compound; a clean, high-floor take.
Temporal Cleansing: Premium blue interaction; pick it early. This convoke-discounted tuck is the format's key UW answer, and 56.1% GIH with +1.4 iwd understates it because GIH underrates removal — the 63.7% play rate shows it always makes the deck. Best in UW Merfolk where convoke fires it near-free, but splashable anywhere blue.
Thirst for Identity: Serviceable blue card-selection/instant. 53.2% GIH with a modest +0.9 IWD makes it a fine role-player that smooths draws in any grindy blue deck — exactly the resource-war filler ECL rewards. Take it middle-of-pack; not a priority but always playable.
Unexpected Assistance: Premium card-advantage. The convoke draw engine doctrine flags as format-defining: 55.8% GIH, 72.9% play rate, castable near-free off a board. In a grindy resource war this is exactly the engine you want. High pick for any deck that fields creatures — most of them.
Unwelcome Sprite: Solid flash faerie for the UB tempo plan. 56.3% GIH with dead-even OH/GD splits marks a consistent, low-variance body that ambushes attackers on the opponent's turn — the Sneakling-style upside the doctrine warns attackers about. Strong role-player in UB Fairies, fine filler elsewhere.
Wanderwine Distracter: Sideboard/filler. 50.9% GIH, negative -1.6 IWD, and a 19.7% play rate — the numbers say the format has correctly benched this. A weak two-drop that gets blanked. Only make the deck if UW Merfolk is desperate for bodies.
Wanderwine Farewell: Solid UW Merfolk playable. 56.8% GIH WR and a healthy GD_WR show it pulls weight as a tribal payoff, but the modest OH_WR marks it as a synergy card, not a standalone slam. Good early-to-mid pick if you're in Merfolk; a filler cut otherwise.
Wild Unraveling: Niche sideboard/role-player instant — 25.1% play rate and 7.2 ALSA say most drafters correctly leave it in the pool. The 53.4% GIH comes from the minority of decks with the right targets. Bring it in against the matchup it answers; don't maindeck it as a default.
Auntie's Sentence: Playable removal-adjacent black common, but underrated by GIH's 53.4% — removal always is. A one-mana-ish debuff/kill effect earns its slot in any black deck; the modest IWD hides that it trades up and holds for lords. Solidly maindeckable, higher pick than the raw number suggests.
Barbed Bloodletter: Filler equipment — 18.4% play rate and a 7.4 ALSA (dead last) tell the story. The 53.4% GIH is a small sample of the few grindy RB decks that wanted it; in a slow, removal-dense format, spending mana to suit up creatures is a losing trade. Sideboard.
Bile-Vial Boggart: Filler. 51.9% GIH and a 6.6 ALSA with sub-43% play rate — this wheels and mostly stays in the sideboard. An RB Goblins body only if you're deep in the tribe and need a blight/drain cog; otherwise it's replacement-level and cuttable.
Bitterbloom Bearer: Premium black mythic. 57.9% GIH with a strong 60.6% OH_WR — it wants to be down early and generate flyers, an aggressive-snowball profile that pairs with UB Fairies/Flash. First-few-picks; the modest GD_WR just means it's best deployed on curve, not topdecked.
Blight Rot: Premium black removal — the format benchmark. 55.4% GIH with +2.4 IWD and 87% play, but remember GIH underrates removal, so it's better than the number. Four -1/-1 counters whiffs on 5-toughness bodies and has hard diminishing returns, so don't overload; still a high pick.
Blighted Blackthorn: Low-end filler. 50.8% GIH and a 28.4% play rate mark it as a marginal Treefolk body most decks cut. The positive drawn WR hints it's better once it's down than in hand, but a five-toughness Warlock aside, it's a replaceable role-player. Only run it in BW Blight if you're short bodies.
Bloodline Bidding: Premium rare and near first-pick. 58.6% GIH, +4.8 IWD, 3.1 ALSA, 76% play — a black recursion/value engine that wins the long resource war this format lives on. The OH/GD split (53.5/61.7) shows it's a mid-to-late haymaker; hold it, don't slam it early.
Boggart Mischief: Strong RB Goblins payoff. 57% GIH and +5.1 iwd, but the drawn/OH gap (58.8 vs 54.7) confirms it needs goblin density to shine — a build-around anthem, not a splash. Premium in grindy RB, near-dead outside it. Take it as a signal you're in Goblins.
Boggart Prankster: Filler common. 52.5% GIH, +0.1 IWD and a telling 44.5% play rate mean most drafters cut it — a marginal Goblin body that only makes the deck when RB is short on playables. Late-pick synergy cog at best; don't count on it.
Bogslither's Embrace: Premium removal — top black common, near-mandatory (88.4% play). One-mana exile when blight is upside; the 56.1% GIH actually underrates it since GIH systematically undervalues efficient removal you don't 'win' by drawing. Take it early over most bodies; it's your interaction spine in any black deck.
Champion of the Weird: Bomb when it sticks — the RB Goblins ceiling card. 59.5% GIH WR and +8.8 IWD, and note the rare inversion where OH_WR (60.1%) tops GD_WR: it's snowballing from turn one. Take it high, protect it, and let it run away with the game.
Creakwood Safewright: Good BG Elves two-drop that actually pulls weight — 57.2% GIH with a 3.7 ALSA and near-symmetric OH/GD (57.3/57.1) means it performs on curve, unusual for a two-drop in this slow format. A synergistic elf cog, not blank filler; solid early pick for the S-tier Elves deck.
Darkness Descends: Sideboard/trap. 49.1% GIH, a dismal 45.9% OH, and 16.7% play rate say this sorcery underperforms and clogs opening hands. The +0.5 IWD is noise on a tiny sample. Situational at best — leave it in the board unless your BW Blight deck has a specific reason.
Dawnhand Dissident: Excellent BG Elves rare and a high pick: 58.9% GIH, +6.2 IWD, 2.3 ALSA. An early Elf Warlock that fits the S-tier deck's graveyard-value plan and comes down before removal matters. Rarely wheels — grab it and commit to BG.
Dawnhand Eulogist: Excellent common — near-uncommon quality. 57.9% GIH with +1.9 IWD and a rising OH-to-GD line marks a BG Elves value engine that's great on curve and better drawn late. Elf typal + graveyard-as-resource is the S-tier deck; prioritize it there, splashable elsewhere.
Dose of Dawnglow: Filler/sideboard. 50.9% GIH, negative -0.7 IWD and a dismal 47.1% OH_WR — a reactive lifegain instant that actively drags your opener and most cut it (38% play). Only a maindeck consideration if BW Blight needs the lifegain buffer; otherwise pass.
Dream Seizer: Niche role-player. 51.3% GIH and a low 27% play rate flag a faerie that only shines in UB Flash/Fairies where its ability matters; the 48.9% OH WR says it's dead early. Speculative pick for that lane only, otherwise a pass.
Gloom Ripper: Bomb — first pick, kill-on-sight if opposing. 66.2% GIH and a monstrous +13.0 iwd at ALSA 2.4 is the best profile in this chunk; it flat-out wins games when drawn. An Elf Assassin that's a slam in BG Elves but a splash-worthy haymaker in any black deck. Take it over everything here.
Gnarlbark Elm: Strong black uncommon body — note the name, this is NOT the trap Narho Bark Elm. 54.0% GIH, +2.4 IWD, 4.1 ALSA, 74% play across a Treefolk Warlock that pulls its weight. Solid grindy playable for any black deck, especially BW Blight or BG Elves.
Graveshifter: Solid playable. A changeling with recursion value: 54% GIH, 87% play rate, and the +5.3pp OH-to-drawn jump shows late-game grind value. Keeps you open (every creature type) and feeds BG Elves graveyard plans. Good glue card — pick over filler bodies, not over removal.
Grub, Storied Matriarch: Strong RB payoff — take it high in Goblins. The 57.8% GIH masks a huge +6.9 IWD and a 60.5% GD>54.0% OH split: this is a grindy engine that overperforms once the board develops, not a turn-one keep. Exactly the RB Goblins go-wide/blight-drain plan; premium there, weaker out of tribe.
Gutsplitter Gang: Mediocre RB Goblins body, a trap for the goblin count. 51.9% GIH and +0.6 IWD are barely playable — this is grindy-goblins filler, not a payoff. Champion of the Weird is what makes RB; this is a body you take late. Skip if not in Goblins.
Heirloom Auntie: Filler/cut. 48.5% GIH WR, -2.4 IWD, ALSA 6.8 — the numbers agree this is a weak two-drop that gets blanked in a format where the two-slot is a trap. Only a late RB Goblins body if you're thin; otherwise leave it in the pack.
Iron-Shield Elf: Replaceable two-drop. Numot nails it: fine elf filler you cut when better options arrive. 57.8% GIH and 59.2% OH read well but this is a BG Elves body that fills a curve slot, not a card you prioritize. Take it mid-pack; expect to trim it in a deep pool.
Moonglove Extractor: Filler leaning cut. 52.1% GIH but a red-flag -1.5 IWD and 41.2% play rate — it's actively worse to draw in most spots, an Elf body without the synergy to justify it. Only a fringe BG Elves inclusion when you need warlocks; otherwise sideboard.
Moonshadow: Strong mythic but front-loaded — note oh_wr 60.5% well above gd_wr 54.8%, so it's best deployed early on curve (2.0 ALSA) rather than topdecked late. An aggressive Elemental that closes games; first-pick-caliber, just play it proactively.
Mornsong Aria: Provisional trap — null WR at 2.8% play rate means almost nobody ran it and it wheels to 6.0. A legendary enchantment build-around that didn't find a home in reps; treat as a sideboard/hate-draft unless you can see the specific engine it rewards. Read is provisional.
Mudbutton Cursetosser: Solid RB Goblins uncommon. 57.5% GIH and a big 60.5% OH_WR mean you want it early doing goblin/blight-drain work — the grindy RB plan, not aggro. Good pick when you're in Goblins; the lower GD_WR says its value is front-loaded on the board.
Nameless Inversion: Best black uncommon and premium removal — first-pick it. 56.4% GIH understates it (GIH underrates removal); +3.1 IWD, 3.1 ALSA, 88% play. A +3/-3 kindred instant that kills nearly anything AND pumps as a trick. Take over almost everything.
Nightmare Sower: Middling uncommon; playable, not a priority. 51.3% GIH with modest +2.8 iwd and a 40.8% play rate says it's a role-player that underperforms its rarity. A Faerie Assassin that fits UB Fairies/Flash for evasive pressure, but it's a mid-pack pick you take when the on-color options thin out.
Perfect Intimidation: Trap/sideboard. 47.4% GIH (below the waterline), -0.5 IWD, and a damning 10.5% play rate — the numbers say almost nobody who tries it keeps it. Conditional removal that whiffs too often; leave it in the pack.
Requiting Hex: Playable removal, unremarkable. 52.7% GIH with a flat +0.9 iwd — GIH famously underrates removal, so trust this is better than it reads, but the conditional nature caps it. Fine black interaction to fill your removal suite; not a first-pick answer like Kinbinding.
Retched Wretch: Below-the-line uncommon. 53.3% GIH with +1.2 IWD and only 56.4% play rate is a replaceable Goblin body — playable when RB needs a creature, cuttable otherwise. Role-player, not a reason to be in the archetype.
Scarblade Scout: Strong BG Elves common, an early-taken cog. 57.4% GIH with 58.3% OH means it pulls its weight from turn one — a well-sized elf that fits the S-tier deck's early-and-late plan. High pick within BG; it's exactly the kind of two-drop that isn't blanked because it has a job.
Scarblade's Malice: Solid black removal-ish playable, underrated by GIH. 54.1% GIH WR with a positive IWD, and per the doctrine removal reads low because it doesn't win by being drawn — value it above its number. A fine instant that fills the removal slot in any black deck; take it earlier than the raw stat suggests.
Shimmercreep: Late-game synergy elemental — the OH/GD split (50.0% opener vs 57.1% drawn) and +4.8 IWD flag it as a card you want to draw into, weak in your opener. A changeling-adjacent body for UR Elementals / Vivid that counts pips. 56.0% play rate; a role-player, not a first-few pick.
Taster of Wares: Premium rare, near-bomb. 60.6% GIH with a matching 60.6% OH and 60.6% GD is remarkably consistent — good early and late, no build-around required. +8.9 IWD and 2.8 ALSA say take it early in any black deck. A slam-dunk playable that overperforms on curve.
Twilight Diviner: Solid BG Elves rare. 56.1% GIH and +3.1 IWD are good-not-broken; the Elf Cleric slots straight into the S-tier graveyard-value deck as a reliable engine piece. High pick within BG, unexciting outside it.
Unbury: Premium uncommon — pick it high. Numot calls it best-in-pack "not close," and 55% GIH with a 51.6% OH / 57.4% GD split confirms an instant you hold for value. Insane in BG Elves for recursion but a strong playable in any tribe-heavy deck. Take over most creatures.
Ashling, Rekindled: Bomb rare. 60.5% GIH, +9.4 IWD, 63.4% OH_WR — an Elemental payoff that dominates from turn one and only gets better, ideal for UR Elementals. Top-end first pick; take it and lean red. Rarely wheels at 80% play.
Boldwyr Aggressor: Aggressive niche uncommon. 51.4% GIH but +2.7 IWD and only 26% play — a giant that wants the RW Blight/Giants beatdown shell (a C-tier lane) and is dead weight elsewhere. Role-player in that deck, low priority overall; the low play rate reflects the archetype's weakness.
Boneclub Berserker: Filler two-plus-drop. 50.5% GIH, negative iwd, ALSA 7.4 — this Goblin wheels because it's a vanilla-ish beater that the grindy RB plan doesn't want. Bad Goblins tries to attack; this is that card. Sideboard-adjacent; only run it if desperate for RB bodies.
Boulder Dash: Premium red removal — Numot flags it splash-worthy and the data agrees: 55.4% GIH, +3.2 IWD, 82% play. As always GIH slightly underrates removal, so value it above the raw number. Take the first two copies high; a third is overkill.
Brambleback Brute: Filler. 52.1% GIH but a 7.0 ALSA, 30.9% play rate, and sub-50 OH_WR mark a curve-filler big body the good decks pass. Playable in a creature-light emergency; the 5-toughness clause helps against burn, but it does nothing proactive. Late-pick material.
Burning Curiosity: Niche card-advantage payoff, NOT a maindeck default. 51.6% GIH, -0.1 IWD and 30.9% play rate say the raw rate is mediocre, but the doctrine prizes the engine it provides — it fills the card-draw hole in RB Goblins. Play one in a built-for-blight Goblins deck; skip it everywhere else, and never run two (hard diminishing returns).
Champion of the Path: Solid UR Elementals rare, good-not-bomb. 54.4% GIH and +4.0 IWD with a 3.1 ALSA — a value engine that rewards the elemental ETB deck rather than dominating alone. Take it as a build-around anchor in UR; the number is honest, not inflated.
Cinder Strike: Premium removal — the best common in the set and a first-pick anchor. The 55.7% GIH WR understates it (GIH chronically underrates efficient removal), and Numot confirms it kills most relevant creatures at instant speed. One-mana deal-4 on blight dodges nothing the format cares about; take it over most rares.
Collective Inferno: Trap rare — the numbers are damning: 48.6% GIH, -1.9 IWD, and only 41.8% play rate for a rare. It wants a built-around board and doesn't deliver; a red enchantment that underperforms replacement-level. Leave it unless your RB/RW deck has an obvious engine for it, and even then be skeptical.
Elder Auntie: Filler. 51.9% GIH, ~0 IWD, 6.7 ALSA — a replacement-level Goblin that the table lets wheel. Plays as a body/cog in RB Goblins go-wide but adds little on its own. Late-pick roster filler, not a card to reach for.
End-Blaze Epiphany: Premium red instant and a strong early pick: 60.2% GIH, +7.8 IWD, 86% play. An instant that plays to the format's off-curve, flash-heavy tempo — hold it up and blow out a combat or push value. Take it high in any red deck.
Enraged Flamecaster: Filler/role-player. 52.8% GIH and 6.6 ALSA — an Elemental body that wheels, only pulling weight in UR Elementals where its type and trigger matter. Outside that tribe it's replacement-level curve filler; take late, cut when your playables firm up.
Explosive Prodigy: Premium Vivid/UR uncommon. 58.0% GIH, +5.6 IWD, 85.4% play — a Vivid payoff that punishes board stalls and thrives in the late game when ahead. High pick in UR Elementals or 2c Vivid; a strong playable even outside them. Prioritize.
Feed the Flames: Premium red removal. Deal-5-and-exile at 54.4% GIH with +2.4 IWD — and GIH underrates removal, so treat it higher. Clean answer to bombs and 5-toughness bodies alike; 80% play confirms it's a staple. High pick in any red deck.
Flame-Chain Mauler: Serviceable red common, upper-filler. 53.2% GIH with a flat iwd makes it a fine curve-filler Elemental Warrior for UR/RB, but nothing to prioritize — the ~52% play rate reflects a replaceable body. Playable when you need bodies; the first card you cut when better cards show up.
Flamebraider: Bomb-adjacent — this is the "Soul Ring" the doctrine says to kill on sight, the engine that carries UR Elementals. 62.7% OH_WR (higher than its drawn WR) means it's a turn-you-want-it-early snowball. First-pick it and pivot UR; ramp/value that breaks games open.
Flamekin Gildweaver: Solid UR Elementals playable. 56.5% GIH and +3.7 iwd with a healthy 67% play rate — the elemental synergy and fixing make it a reliable midrange cog. Not flashy but consistently good in its lane. Take over generic filler when you're in Elementals or Vivid.
Giantfall: Serviceable red removal, slightly underrated by GIH. 53.4% GIH with +2.0 IWD and 64.2% play rate reads as a widely-run answer that keeps you alive — remember removal is undervalued by these numbers. Not premium (it's conditional/giant-flavored), but a solid maindeck pick for any red deck.
Goatnap: Trap / near-unplayable. 48.4% GIH, 43.1% OH, and a 5.5% play rate — the format has emphatically rejected it. A slow one-shot threaten effect in a grindy format where it does nothing on defense. Leave it in the pack.
Goliath Daydreamer: Solid red rare, take it. 55.2% GIH WR with an early ALSA of 2.7 — the table respects it. A midrange body with wizard/giant upside that plays well in UR Elementals and any red deck; not a format-warper but a comfortable high pick.
Gristle Glutton: Mediocre red common goblin — 53.8% GIH, +0.9 IWD, a 6.4 ALSA and 60.7% play rate mark it as marginal curve-filler. RB Goblins wants density but this is a body you take late. Playable in the tribe, cuttable everywhere else; not a reason to be in red.
Hexing Squelcher: Underwhelming rare — trap-adjacent. Despite a 3.2 ALSA (drafters take it high on name/rarity), it posts a flat 50.7% GIH and -0.6 IWD, i.e. replacement-level. A Goblin Sorcerer whose disruption doesn't move games; playable in RB but do not prioritize it over real removal or payoffs.
Impolite Entrance: Trap — the numbers are damning. 43.6% GIH, -4.5 IWD, and a 9.8% play rate mean it actively loses games and almost nobody keeps it. A sorcery that doesn't move the board in a grindy format. Leave it in the sideboard.
Kindle the Inner Flame: Synergy payoff, not a slam — the numbers come from the built-around deck. 55.3% GIH but a 51% OH / 58% GD split and 40% play rate: a kindred sorcery that's dead without Elemental density. Good in UR Elementals, mediocre elsewhere. Speculative early, strong once committed.
Kulrath Zealot: Above-average red common. 56.7% GIH and +4.0 IWD is a genuinely good rate for a common — an Elemental Warrior cog that pulls its weight in UR/aggressive red. Solid early-mid pick, better than its 5.4 ALSA suggests; take it before the filler two-drops.
Lasting Tarfire: Trap. 46.9% GIH, -3.5 IWD, 43.9% OH WR — an enchantment that reads better than it plays and drags games down. Only 33% play. Sideboard-tier; don't be seduced by the ceiling, the reps say it's bad.
Lavaleaper: Trap rare — leave it. 48.6% GIH, negative iwd, and a damning 11.2% play rate say the format has tried it and passed; the rarity symbol is the only exciting thing here. A vanilla-ish Elemental that doesn't impact the board enough. Take a solid common over it every time.
Meek Attack: Provisional, and provisionally a trap — 0.9% play rate at mythic means essentially nobody drafts it, so the null GIH is a non-signal. A build-around enchantment that wants a weenie-attack shell ECL's grind punishes (see last-place GW). Sideboard curio only.
Reckless Ransacking: Trap/sideboard. 50.1% GIH, 10.7% play rate, 7.8 ALSA — the numbers scream a card the field correctly avoids. Rummage-style effects tempt in a resource format but this one doesn't clear the bar. Leave it unless you specifically need the filtering; low priority.
Scuzzback Scrounger: Strong red rare, take it early. 55.1% GIH looks modest but 3.1 ALSA and 84.3% play rate show it's an every-deck body, and the 57.2% OH>53.5% GD split marks it as a proactive early threat with grindy recursion. Excellent in RB Goblins; a fine aggressive two/three elsewhere.
Sear: Premium removal — best-in-class clean deal-4 (kills through the 5-toughness wall), 90.4% play rate confirms it's a slam. 56.7% GIH under-sells it because GIH undervalues removal; the +4.3 IWD and 2.9 ALSA are the real story. First-pick-caliber in any red deck; hold it for lords and flash finishers.
Sizzling Changeling: Solid playable and format-flexible. 54.1% GIH WR with an 83% play rate — a changeling body that satisfies every typal payoff (Goblins, Elementals) and keeps you open early in the draft. Better than a vanilla two-drop precisely because it's every creature type; take it and stay flexible.
Soul Immolation: First-pick bomb removal. 63.2% GIH, +11.9 IWD, 2.2 ALSA — a red mythic sorcery that dominates whenever drawn (66.0% GD). This is your P1 in any red deck and a strong reason to move in; it kills the format's big threats. Take over almost anything.
Soulbright Seeker: Solid playable, aggressive-leaning. 55.1% GIH with 56.6% OH beating its 54.2% GD marks it as a proactive early body you'd rather have turn one — an Elemental Sorcerer for UR. Good but front-loaded; the +1.5 IWD says it's a fine role-player, not a bomb.
Sourbread Auntie: Solid RB Goblins playable. 55.3% GIH with a 4.9 ALSA marks it as a good tribal cog for the B-tier grindy Goblin deck built on blight-drain and triggers, not a beater. Fine mid-pick when you're in RB; skippable otherwise.
Spinerock Tyrant: Bomb — first pick, no debate. 61.8% GIH, +11.5 IWD, 1.8 ALSA and flat 61/62 OH/GD: a dragon that dominates regardless of deck or timing. This is the pick over anything short of format-defining removal. Kill-on-sight from the other side.
Squawkroaster: Marginal red uncommon. 51.9% GIH, +2.1 IWD and 48.7% play put it at replaceable-body level — an Elemental that fills a slot without moving the needle. Playable in a shallow UR pool, first cut when the deck comes together. Let it wheel.
Sting-Slinger: Marginal RB goblin. 52.1% GIH with a flat -0.3 IWD says it's a body that doesn't advance your position. RB Goblins is a grindy B-tier lane and this is filler within it — playable cog, not a reason to be in the color. Late pick.
Tweeze: Solid red playable — take it fairly high. 54.6% GIH, +2.0 iwd, 82.6% play rate at ALSA 4.5 shows the format reliably wants this instant. Flexible, efficient, and it plays to the off-curve/flash instinct the format rewards. Good in UR and RB; a dependable maindeck pick.
Warren Torchmaster: Filler Goblin. 51.1% GIH with -1.2 IWD and a flat OH/GD split says it does nothing on its own — a body that only matters in RB Goblins go-wide, and even there it's a middling cog. Playable in-tribe, cuttable everywhere else.
Assert Perfection: Premium green playable. 57.9% GIH, +3.2 iwd, 89% play rate, 3.9 ALSA — this is a reliable, near-auto-include that pulls its weight in every green deck. Efficient and format-friendly. High pick; one of the better green commons here.
Aurora Awakener: Bomb — slam it. 60.6% GIH, a massive +10.5 IWD, 1.7 ALSA and 90.7% play rate is elite: a green mythic that takes over any game it lands. The GD>OH gap just means it's even better once you've hit land drops. First-pick.
Bloom Tender: Overrated by name, solid but not a Limited bomb here. 54.3% GIH with OH (57.3%) beating GD (52.0%) says it's best as early ramp/fixing that gets worse in topdeck wars. Great enabler for BG Elves and any greedy/splashy build, but the actual win-rate is good-playable, not first-pick-lock.
Blossoming Defense: Premium green trick. 55.6% GIH WR and a 79% play rate for a one-mana protect-and-pump that answers removal AND wins combat, exactly the off-curve flash play the format rewards. The low IWD is normal for a reactive card — value it on GIH. High pick in any green deck.
Bristlebane Battler: Excellent aggressive green rare — 63.6% OH_WR and a 2.0 ALSA scream a proactive threat best in your opener, which fits its WG Kithkin / GW aggro home. The OH>GD split (63.6 vs 56.9) says play it early and beat down. High pick; anchors the aggressive green decks.
Bristlebane Outrider: Strong green uncommon. 56.1% GIH, 4.4 ALSA and 72% play — a well-sized Kithkin Knight that overperforms as a beater. Best in GW Kithkin but generically good in any green deck. Solid-to-premium playable; take it reasonably early.
Celestial Reunion: Overrated by rarity — this mythic sorcery posts only 53.7% GIH and a flat +0.7 IWD at 48.8% play, so it's a build-around that underdelivers for a bomb slot. Don't first-pick it on the symbol; treat it as a conditional playable and take proven cards ahead of it.
Champions of the Perfect: Bomb-tier rare. 61% GIH with +8.3 IWD and 2.0 ALSA — an Elf warrior that wins games by itself and anchors S-tier BG Elves. Flat OH/GD means it's great early and closes late. Take P1; it's a top-of-the-set body.
Chomping Changeling: Trap/late playable. 49.3% GIH and a red-flag -3.3 IWD — the worst kind of changeling, a body whose typal upside doesn't cover a bad rate. Only run it if a tribe desperately needs the type-count; otherwise it's a curve-filler you cut. Provisional but the -3.3 is damning.
Crossroads Watcher: Solid GW/kithkin common. 55.3% GIH and a healthy 55.6% OH WR mark a real early contributor, not a synergy-only card. Good body for the Kithkin/Vivid green base; comfortable mid-pack pick with a high floor.
Dawn's Light Archer: Reach role-player; playable green common. 54.8% GIH but negative iwd means its value is defensive — an Elf Archer whose reach blanks fliers and ambushes attackers into open mana, exactly the format's flash-tax pattern. Fine in BG/WG, but it's a body you play, not a pick you reach for.
Dundoolin Weaver: Excellent green uncommon and an early pick — 56.1% GIH, 3.5 ALSA, 87.7% play is elite ubiquity for a mana/value Druid that fits GW Kithkin, BG Elves, and Vivid ramp alike. The modest +1.5 IWD reflects it being an enabler, not a bomb, but take it high.
Formidable Speaker: Strong BG Elves rare. 57.6% GIH with identical OH/drawn WR (57.6 across the board) means it's good whenever you have it, curve-independent — a stable early-drop payoff. The 2.0 ALSA is deserved. Priority pick in elves; a fine value creature anywhere green.
Gilt-Leaf's Embrace: Mediocre aura, near the maindeck cut line. 54.9% GIH but +0.4 IWD and 43.8% play rate flag a card most drafters leave out — an aura that pumps/enables but risks two-for-one blowouts. A situational Elf (BG) role-player; take removal and bodies over it.
Great Forest Druid: Above-average green common, a real playable. 54% GIH and OH>GD (56.3 vs 52.2) — a 5-toughness-adjacent body that's better early as a blocker/ramp than late. Treefolk toughness helps it dodge removal and hold the ground the format grinds over. Comfortable maindeck in BG/GW.
Luminollusk: Fringe playable, provisional lean toward cut. 51.1% GIH WR and a poor 47.4% OH_WR mark it as a clunky midgame body you'd rather draw than open. The +1.6 IWD keeps it from filler, but it's a late green pick, not a priority — take real cards first.
Lys Alana Dignitary: Solid BG Elves uncommon — 57.6% GIH with balanced OH/GD (58.9/56.6) and a 4.1 ALSA make it a dependable elf value creature. Not flashy but a real synergy cog for the S-tier Elves deck; a comfortable mid-pack pick that plays every game.
Lys Alana Informant: Excellent green common, a BG Elves cornerstone. 56.9% GIH and 83.8% play with a friendly 4.9 ALSA means it's a high-floor Elf that tables less than you'd like. Prioritize in the S-tier Elves deck; it's the kind of synergistic two/three that actually holds up in the grind.
Midnight Tilling: Role-player, not a game-swinger — +0.4 IWD says it barely changes games when drawn, and the 56.3% GIH reflects decks that used it as green fixing/utility. A 6.7-ALSA wheeler you play when you need the smoothing, not a card to prioritize.
Mistmeadow Council: Top common, prioritize it. 56.6% GIH from a Kithkin advisor that's really a card-advantage engine — the archetype-agnostic value ECL prizes (see doctrine's engine emphasis). Good in any grindy GW/Kithkin or Vivid build; the +1.9 IWD confirms it earns its slot. High common pick.
Moon-Vigil Adherents: Strong green uncommon, near-premium. 58.6% GIH, 3.2 ALSA and 88.7% play — an Elf Druid the BG Elves deck (the S-tier archetype) always wants for density and mana. High pick; the reason it plays everywhere is it's a great cog. Take early.
Morcant's Eyes: Near-best non-rare in the set — a bomb-tier BG Elves engine. 60.4% GIH, +4.4 IWD, 61.8% drawn. Floods 2/2 elf tokens as a grindy late-game resource that BG dominates with. First-pick it and commit to BG Elves (the S-tier deck).
Mutable Explorer: Strong, flexible rare — high pick. The ALSA of 2.6 and 81.4% play rate show it's taken early and always played; 54.1% GIH is a touch soft but a Shapeshifter changeling keeps you open, counts for every typal payoff, and fixes/ramps. Premium for its flexibility across BG, WG, and Vivid.
Pitiless Fists: Premium green aura — yes, an aura that actually earns it: 58.5% GIH, +3.8 IWD, 88% play. It reads as removal-via-combat plus evasion and the numbers back a near-first-pick verdict. Rare exception to "auras are card disadvantage"; slam it in any green deck.
Prismabasher: Premium Vivid payoff. 56.5% GIH, +4.8 iwd, and the OH-to-drawn jump (52.5→59.2) confirm it's a late-game Vivid crusher, not an on-curve slam. Best in 2c Vivid where off-color pips fuel it. Strong pick when building Vivid, merely playable otherwise.
Prismatic Undercurrents: Trap — the five-color-fixing card the doctrine explicitly warns against. 48.9% GIH (sub-50), 45.4% OH and 21.9% play rate confirm it: over-fixing that pushes you toward the losing Prismatic pile. Vivid is a strict TWO-color deck; leave this in the box.
Pummeler for Hire: Trap — the poster child for 'big top-end with no board impact.' 55.6% GIH looks fine but the gap (52.6% OH, 57.6% GD) shows it only shines when you're already stabilizing; guides literally 'wish it had a home.' A vanilla-ish giant that loses to the grind. Low priority, cut when you have better fillers.
Safewright Cavalry: Solid green common. 56.2% GIH WR is strong for a common Elf Warrior — a well-sized body that pulls double duty in BG Elves and any green deck. The low IWD just means it's a proactive early play; take it as reliable curve-filler with tribal upside.
Sapling Nursery: Good green rare engine — 56.4% GIH with +4.6 IWD and a strong 2.7 ALSA for an enchantment signals a token/board engine that grinds well. Fits GW Kithkin go-wide or a Vivid base wanting bodies. Take it fairly early as an engine; it earns the resource war.
Selfless Safewright: Premium green rare. 56.4% GIH undersells it — +3.0 IWD, 2.3 ALSA and 58.5% GD show a protective Elf that shines once it's on the board defending your engines. Great in BG Elves and any green deck; take early, and note the number is dragged by early-game clunk, not late impact.
Shimmerwilds Growth: Vivid enabler, priced by that role — a middling 50.2% GIH and +0.3 IWD in a vacuum, but this is the named Vivid-count booster (Shimmer Wild's Growth) that turns on Shine Striker, Prisma Basher, and friends. Only draft it if you're committed to the A-minus 2c Vivid deck; otherwise it's a do-nothing aura.
Spry and Mighty: Solid playable trick, not a bomb despite rare. 53.6% GIH with a 50.6% OH / 55.7% GD split — a combat sorcery you want drawn with a board, dead in your opener. Fine in aggressive GW/Kithkin, but don't overvalue the rarity; it's a mid-pick pump/removal-ish effect.
Surly Farrier: Filler Kithkin common. 53.7% GIH but -1.0 IWD and 6.1 ALSA mark it as a replaceable two/three-drop body — fine in a WG Kithkin curve, dead weight elsewhere. The negative IWD warns you not to overvalue it; a late pick and an easy cut.
Tend the Sprigs: Filler/build-around sorcery. 49.6% GIH, sub-46% OH WR, and 22% play mark a slow card that wants a dedicated go-wide/token green shell to justify. Provisional playable in that build only; otherwise a pass — the low play rate says most drafters correctly cut it.
Thoughtweft Charge: Role-player combat trick. 54.2% GIH with a flat +0.2 iwd is the classic trick profile — swings a fight but doesn't generate advantage. A 62% play rate says green decks run it; fine in WG Kithkin or BG Elves as a tempo trick, but don't overvalue it. Mid-pick.
Trystan, Callous Cultivator: First-pick bomb for BG Elves and green generally. 60.6% GIH, +6.3 IWD, 2.5 ALSA, 84% play with near-symmetric OH/GD — an elf-payoff engine that's great early and late, exactly the S-tier lane. Take it over almost anything.
Unforgiving Aim: Sideboard combat trick. 51.2% GIH but a negative -0.9 iwd and 21% play rate — the classic trap trick that loses cards more than it wins them in a flash-dense format. Only for aggressive GW Kithkin blowouts, and even then marginal. Leave in the pool.
Vinebred Brawler: Solid green body, unspectacular. 55.9% GIH but a flat +0.7 IWD means it's a fine on-curve Elf (BG) creature that doesn't swing games by itself — good deck-filler with tribal upside. Playable at a decent clip; not a card to prioritize over engines or removal.
Virulent Emissary: Premium BG Elves common/uncommon — high pick. 58.3% GIH, 88.8% play, strong across OH and GD (59.2/57.6) means it performs in every phase, the hallmark of a real card, not a synergy payoff. An elf assassin that fits the S-tier deck perfectly; take it early.
Wildvine Pummeler: Fringe/filler. 51.9% GIH WR and a weak 48.4% OH_WR flag a top-heavy Giant that reads better than it plays — the doctrine's warning on big vanilla-ish bodies losing to the grind applies. The +2.8 IWD is real, so it's a playable in a curve-hungry green deck, but a late pick.
Abigale, Eloquent First-Year: Premium WB gold bomb — a 92.9% play rate and 1.7 ALSA mean nobody passes her, and 60.3% GD backs it up. A legendary bird bard that overperforms in BW Blight's grind. First-pick when in the colors and a strong signal to be in WB; +5.2 IWD confirms she swings games.
Ashling's Command: Best card in the chunk — format-defining bomb. 66.1% GIH and a monstrous +14.8 IWD on a modal Elemental instant; on-color Commands are the ceiling of the set. First-pick, sign you into UR Elementals. If you can cast it, you play it — no questions.
Boggart Cursecrafter: Strong RB Goblins uncommon: 57.0% GIH and +4.9 IWD show it carries games in the grindy Goblin build. A Goblin Warlock that fuels blight/drain triggers — a high pick once you're in RB, and better than the tribe's B tier suggests.
Bre of Clan Stoutarm: Strong gold rare — high pick in RW. +6.4 IWD and 55.8% GIH with a 53.6% OH / 57.1% GD split: a Giant that snowballs when it sticks, powering RW Blight/Giants beatdown. C-tier archetype so it's build-dependent, but the card itself overperforms — take it and commit RW.
Brigid's Command: Premium WG gold rare. 59.8% GIH, +6.4 IWD — a flexible modal Command, top-tier when on-color for Kithkin. But WG finished LAST retro, so it's a signal to be in a struggling archetype; take the power, stay wary of committing hard to Kithkin. Strong when it's your lane.
Catharsis: Strong RW mythic incarnation — take it, but it's not format-warping. 53.1% GIH looks modest, yet 2.1 ALSA and 77% play show drafters value the ceiling; the +2.6 IWD/55.2% drawn split says it plays better once resolved than in openers. First-pickable, splashable payoff for aggressive builds.
Chaos Spewer: Below-average Goblin filler. 50.4% GIH, negative iwd, 39.6% play rate — a marginal RB body that the grindy plan tolerates rather than wants. Playable only in Goblins when you need to fill out the curve; otherwise it's near the bottom of your list.
Chitinous Graspling: Filler changeling — counts as every type and holds you open, but the numbers are flat (51.0% GIH, -0.6 IWD, 46% play). A serviceable typal cog for UG/Vivid or any tribe short on bodies, not a card you prioritize. Wheel-and-take material.
Deceit: Bomb — first pick. 58.9% GIH, +7.5 iwd, 1.7 ALSA, 87% play rate: a UB mythic Incarnation that dominates. The stats undersell mythics if anything; slam it and build around it. One of the best cards you'll open in this chunk.
Deepchannel Duelist: Premium — the UW Merfolk payoff lord and a near-bomb. 63.3% GIH, +8.9 IWD and a 64.0% OH WR mean it's a snowballing tempo engine that closes games. The doctrine names it THE payoff for the A-tier Merfolk deck; first-pick-quality when you're in WU.
Deepway Navigator: Good UW Merfolk rare, solid not spectacular. 56.3% GIH is even across OH/GD (56.5/56.2), an honest workhorse rather than a bomb — reliable evasion/tempo for the convoke plan. High pick in Merfolk; not a splash-worthy game-ender.
Doran, Besieged by Time: Bomb, especially in Abzan/BG Elves or BW Blight shells. 58.5% GIH WR but the eye-popping number is +10.9 IWD — drawing it swings games hard, and toughness-matters here rewards the format's fat bodies. Splashable across WBG; take it very high and build toward the three colors.
Dream Harvest: Underwhelming UB rare — 50.3% GIH, +0.8 IWD and a poor 45.6% OH_WR (dead early) with only 51.4% play rate. A sorcery-speed engine that's clunky and slow even in UB Fairies/Flash. Playable if your deck is built to exploit it, but it's a middling pick, not a bomb.
Eclipsed Boggart: Strong gold uncommon that beats the Eclipsed skepticism. 58.9% GIH and +6.2 IWD say this one's a hit even though the cycle was community-overrated — it delivers in RB Goblins/blight. Take it as a high pick when in BR; the density concern is real elsewhere, but the live numbers are clean.
Eclipsed Elf: Premium BG Elves uncommon — the Eclipse card that actually delivers. 63.0% GIH, +8.1 IWD, 83% play; note oh_wr and gd_wr are both 63%, so it's good whenever you draw it. An early Elf Scout in the S-tier deck; take it very high.
Eclipsed Flamekin: Premium uncommon for UR — pick it high. 59.9% GIH and +6.7 IWD with a flat 59/60 line: unusually, this Eclipse card actually delivers, meaning it's finding its 12+ hits in Elementals. The best of the overrated Eclipse cycle by the numbers. Prioritize in UR Elementals.
Eclipsed Kithkin: Best card in this chunk by rate — 62.4% GIH, +7.7 IWD, 64.5% OH_WR. Unlike most overrated Eclipsed cards this one delivers, but the numbers come from the built-around WG Kithkin shell; decode that the read is inflated toward the density deck. Still a high pick — just verify you have the hits.
Eclipsed Merrow: Elite UW uncommon — an Eclipsed card that actually delivers. 61.8% GIH, +6.8 IWD, and identical OH/GD WR mean it's great in openers AND topdecks, dodging the 'wants density' Eclipse caveat. Premium merfolk payoff; take it very early in UW.
Emptiness: Mythic bomb — first-pickable, ALSA 1.6 says nobody lets it wheel. 56.8% GIH with +5.6 iwd and an 87% play rate is strong; the OH/GD split (53.6/59.0) shows it snowballs the longer the game goes, ideal for grindy BW Blight. Slam it and build around it.
Feisty Spikeling: Below-average changeling despite decent 60.8% play — 50.7% GIH and -1.8 IWD say the body doesn't pull weight, so it's here for typal counting in RW Blight/Giants, not stats. Playable filler that keeps you tribally flexible; take it late.
Figure of Fable: Bomb — the highest pick here. 63.6% GIH, +10.6 iwd, 65.5% OH_WR, 94% play rate: a GW Kithkin rare that wins on curve and grinds. Even though Kithkin finished last as an archetype, this individual card is elite. Take it over nearly everything.
Flaring Cinder: Solid UR Elemental common. 55.2% GIH with +2.1 IWD and 60.4% play rate is a dependable body/enabler for the elementals midrange plan (UR). Not flashy, but a real playable that supports the ETB/late-game gameplan; take it mid-pack for the archetype.
Gangly Stompling: Changeling filler that's better than its stats suggest for keeping open. 53.7% GIH, flat +0.4 IWD — a vanilla-ish shapeshifter body, but as a changeling it counts for every tribe and Vivid pips. Playable glue in RG/Vivid or any tribal deck short on bodies; never a priority pick.
Glister Bairn: Fringe UG playable. 52.3% GIH WR with a weak OH_WR and modest IWD marks a synergy cog, not a standalone card, and UG isn't a supported tribe — it's a Vivid/splash body at best. Playable if your colors line up, but don't prioritize; take real cards first.
Grub's Command: Top-tier RB Goblins gold card — 62.7% GIH, +11.8 IWD, and a modal Goblin command that does everything the grindy Goblins deck wants. Take it very early when in RB; a near-bomb payoff. The 70.2% play rate is only capped by needing to be in the pair — if you're RB, it's a P1-P2.
High Perfect Morcant: Bomb-tier rare and a BG Elves payoff lord. 61.8% GIH, +9.1 IWD, 2.3 ALSA — an Elf Noble that snowballs the best deck in the format. First-pick in Elves, and strong enough to move you into BG. Slam whenever you're in green-black.
Hovel Hurler: Solid playable that gets better as games grind — gd_wr 55.5% beats oh_wr 49.3%, so it's a late-game body, not an opener. A Giant for the C-tier RW Blight/Giants beatdown; a fine 3.9-ALSA cog but the archetype is unrefined, so don't overvalue.
Kirol, Attentive First-Year: Modest gold rare — playable, not exciting. 52.7% GIH and +0.5 IWD despite 81% play rate: a legend people run on sight that barely moves win rate, the classic "looks better than it plays" trap. Fine RW filler if you're already there; not a reason to be in the colors.
Lluwen, Imperfect Naturalist: Premium BG rare. 58.8% GIH, +6.3 IWD, 2.3 ALSA and 85.6% play — an Elf Druid engine for the S-tier BG Elves deck, best-early-and-late format's crown. First-few-picks and commit to BG; it almost never wheels.
Maralen, Fae Ascendant: Bomb — first-pick, first-pick. 60.4% GIH with a massive +10.3 IWD and 2.5 ALSA; the huge improvement-when-drawn is the signature of a game-winning engine. Sultai-shaded but pushes you toward BG/UB. Take over nearly anything in the set.
Merrow Skyswimmer: Very good UW common — pick it early. 57.1% GIH, +2.5 iwd, 81.6% play rate marks it a premium Merfolk cog for the A-tier tempo/convoke deck. It's a body that pulls its weight both early and late. High priority when you're in blue-white.
Mischievous Sneakling: The best common changeling — a premium flash ambusher, and the doctrine's headline threat to "not slam attacks into open mana." 52.4% GIH understates it because ambush value doesn't show in drawn WR; 75% play tells the real story. High pick, especially UB Flash.
Morcant's Loyalist: Premium BG Elves uncommon. 61.3% GIH and +6.8 iwd with an early 3.1 ALSA — a well-sized elf that's exactly what the S-tier deck wants. Strong in the best archetype; a high pick and a clear elves signal. Prioritize when in BG.
Noggle Robber: Strong RG uncommon, overperforms its floor. 57.3% GIH with +4.6 IWD and 81.8% play rate marks a genuinely good gold two-color card — the tempo/value it brings serves the Temur Vivid base (RG). High pick whenever you're in those colors.
Prideful Feastling: Below-average changeling body. 52.9% GIH, +0.1 IWD — the shapeshifter type gives it universal tribal/Vivid utility, but the raw card is weak. Take it late as flex glue for a tribe or Vivid pip count; first cut when your bodies are better.
Raiding Schemes: Trap/sideboard — provisional, null GIH WR. The 2.4% play rate and 6.1 ALSA scream unplayed niche enchantment, and RG barely exists as a pure pair in this format (it's a Temur Vivid base). Read is unbuilt-around; leave it unless you have a specific engine. Skip.
Reaping Willow: Strong BW Blight engine — the OH/GD split (53.2 opener / 59.3 drawn) plus +5.0 IWD shows a recursive treefolk you want mid-to-late, absorbing counters and coming back. A key cog for the blight-as-upside deck; a high pick in WB and a signal to commit. 79.6% play rate for an uncommon is telling.
Sanar, Innovative First-Year: Bomb. 60.4% GIH, +8.0 IWD, a near-universal 92.6% play rate and 2.0 ALSA — it's taken high and delivers. A legendary Goblin Sorcerer anchoring UR; the 61.5% GD says it's even better drawn into the mid-game. First-pick, wheels to nobody.
Shadow Urchin: Underwhelming rare — 53.7% GIH is barely above filler for the symbol, and the early 2.9 ALSA reflects hype more than payoff. A fine RB Ouphe body that fits Goblins/blight, but don't pass real removal or a bomb for it. Playable, not a slam.
Stoic Grove-Guide: Trap-adjacent filler — the -3.1 IWD is a red flag. A BG Elf druid that's actively worse to draw, meaning it's a do-nothing body clogging your deck. Only a mana/ramp cog if you specifically need it; the 52.6% GIH is deck-carried, not card-earned. Cut aggressively.
Sygg's Command: Premium UW gold rare. 58.7% GIH, +5.2 IWD — a flexible Merfolk Command, top-tier on-color for A-tier UW Merfolk, the highest-floor deck in the set. Strong pick that signals a good lane; take it and lean UW tempo.
Tam, Mindful First-Year: Strong UG rare, taken universally (93% play, 2.1 ALSA) but the +1.0 IWD and 53.7% GIH say it's a good value creature, not a bomb — solid rather than back-breaking. First-pick-worthy for the body and flexibility; just don't expect it to win on its own.
Thoughtweft Lieutenant: Strong Kithkin payoff; high pick in WG. 58.8% GIH with a 59.8% opening-hand WR and +4.3 iwd means it performs immediately — good news for the fragile aggro deck. It's a genuine lord-style engine for WG weenie; the caveat is WG finished last, so it's only great when the tribe comes together.
Trystan's Command: Top-tier gold bomb — 63.7% GIH and a staggering +11.3 IWD, the best numbers in this chunk, anchoring BG Elves (the S-tier deck). A modal Command that does everything; the 2.2 ALSA means it's snapped up. First-pick when you're in or near BG.
Twinflame Travelers: Strong UR Elementals uncommon. 57.2% GIH, +4.9 iwd, 80% play rate — the ETB-power midrange plan the A- deck is built on. Reliable value in Elementals; a good pick that reinforces your lane. Solid but replaceable outside UR.
Vibrance: Bomb — first-pick. 61.5% GIH, +10.0 IWD, 1.7 ALSA and 89.6% play rate is the elite mythic signature. An Elemental Incarnation that dominates the board; take it over almost everything and let it define your RG/Temur base.
Voracious Tome-Skimmer: UB Fairies/Flash payoff — the archetype's card-draw engine, and its numbers are deceptive. Low 36% play rate but +3.7 IWD and 52.9% GIH come almost entirely from the built-around UB flash deck. In that seat it's a high pick that draws you ahead; outside it, unplayable. Decode before you take.
Wary Farmer: Solid GW Kithkin common. 54.8% GIH WR with perfectly flat OH/GD splits — a dependable, no-nonsense body that does the same job whenever you draw it. Good curve-filler for the weenie plan; take it as a role-player, not a priority, since GW finished last as an archetype.
Wistfulness: First-pick UG mythic bomb — 92.4% play rate, 1.6 ALSA, +9.5 IWD: an elemental incarnation nobody passes. Slots into UR Elementals / UG Vivid but strong enough to splash. 62.0% GD_WR means it wins the games it's drawn. Slam it and build around the colors.
Chronicle of Victory: Colorless bomb — the best kind. 62.3% GIH, +9.7 IWD, 1.2 ALSA and 98.4% play: it goes in every deck and gets taken P1P1. A legendary artifact engine that fits any archetype. Auto-first-pick, no color commitment required.
Dawn-Blessed Pennant: Fixing artifact — the -0.5 IWD confirms it does nothing the turn you draw it; its value is enabling splashes and Vivid bases. 53.8% GIH comes from decks that needed the smoothing. Take it only when your mana demands it, late.
Firdoch Core: Fringe artifact — 50.8% GIH, 6.5 ALSA, 28% play rate: it wheels and mostly warms the sideboard. A changeling-shapeshifter cog that ticks typal boxes but does little on board; only maindeck if you need to satisfy kindred payoffs. Replacement-level; take last.
Foraging Wickermaw: Playable colorless common. 53.6% GIH and +2.5 IWD is a respectable rate for a Scarecrow changeling body that slots any deck and any tribe. A fine flexible early pick that keeps you open; not exciting, but honest curve-filler with typal upside. Let it wheel if colored cogs are on the table.
Gathering Stone: Premium colorless fixing/ramp — plays in every deck. 58.3% GIH, +3.6 IWD, 87% play at 3.8 ALSA. Enables splashes (Catharsis, off-color bombs) and Vivid bases while smoothing curve. High pick that keeps you open early; snap it up.
Mirrormind Crown: Trap — do not play. 39.4% GIH and a brutal -7.4 iwd with a 5.2% play rate is one of the worst profiles in the set; the colorless equipment does nothing to affect the board in a grindy format. Leave it in the box regardless of the rare symbol.
Puca's Eye: Vivid enabler / role-player. 54.6% GIH and a fat +5.0 IWD but only 24% play and a late 6.9 ALSA — it's a colorless fixing/pip artifact that overperforms specifically in two-color Vivid, doing little elsewhere. Take it if you're building Vivid; skip otherwise.
Springleaf Drum: Sideboard fixing. 50.0% GIH, negative -0.5 iwd, 24.6% play rate — mana rocks that don't advance the board underperform in this grindy format. Only for a splash-heavy Vivid or convoke shell that needs the fixing/tap enabler. Low priority; most decks skip it.
Stalactite Dagger: Filler equipment, usually a cut. 51.3% GIH, -0.7 IWD and 21.6% play rate say the equipment tax rarely pays off in this grindy format. Sideboard/aggro-only role-player; don't maindeck it unless you're desperate for cheap threats in a go-wide WG or RB shell.
Blood Crypt: Fixing land, take it for the deck you're building not for power. 52.4% GIH and flat IWD are what a dual land looks like — it enables RB Goblins or any black-red splash without costing a card. Solid utility pick, higher if you're multicolor or splashing removal; not a bomb.
Eclipsed Realms: Playable utility land, provisional value. 53.7% GIH WR and 67% play rate say the fixing/late-game mode earns a slot, but it's a colorless land — the number rides on smoothing, not power. Fine to run in a two-color deck wanting reach; don't draft it over spells.
Evolving Wilds: Premium fixing — 93.9% play rate says everyone runs it, and this format's two-color tribal and Vivid bases love the enable. The 54.5% GIH is inflated by being in every good deck. Take it when you need fixing, especially for a splash or a Vivid base; a reliable early-to-mid pick, not a bomb.
Hallowed Fountain: Fixing, not a payoff. 52.9% GIH with 54.5% OH over 51.7% GD is exactly a dual land's profile — great early, dead later. Take it to enable a UW base or a splash; don't overvalue the rarity. A useful role-player for two-color and Vivid manabases, nothing more.
Overgrown Tomb: Good fixing for BG Elves — a dual land that comes in untapped and enables the S-tier deck plus any black/green splash. Flat +0.0 IWD is normal for a land; the 54.2% GIH reflects the strong decks running it. Reasonable early pick if you're leaning BG.
Steam Vents: Fixing for UR — a solid utility pick, not a spell. 53% GIH just tracks that dual lands smooth two-color decks; the value is enabling UR Elementals and Vivid bases, not winning games. Take it when your manabase needs it, especially splashing or in a Vivid two-color pile.
Temple Garden: Solid fixing rare, not a bomb. 52.7% GIH and -0.7 IWD are unremarkable because a dual land does nothing on the battlefield — its value is enabling a two-color base (Vivid, WG, BG). Take it in the right colors as a high-floor fixer; it's a wheel-friendly luxury, not a slam.
Idyllic Tutor: Provisional read (null GIH). A tutor is only as good as your best enchantment target, and ECL's commons aren't worth searching — the 5% play rate confirms nobody found a home. Likely a trap in Limited; sideboard/pass unless you have a true enchantment bomb.
Kinsbaile Cavalier: Provisional read (null GIH): a double-strike-granting Kithkin lord, this is a WG payoff whose ceiling is high but whose deck finished last and folds to one removal spell. ALSA 4.0 and 53.8% play rate suggest people take it as a build-around. Speculative early pick only if you're committed to WG Kithkin; otherwise a trap.
Mistbind Clique: Provisional — null GIH but 49.3% play at a 3.4 ALSA (people take it early) signals a real flash faerie payoff, not a dud. The classic tapper/tempo rare wants UW Merfolk or UB Flash. Read is provisional, but pedigree and pick position say solid-to-strong; draft it into flash.
Wanderwine Prophets: Null GIH WR — read is provisional. This UW Merfolk rare is a marquee champion payoff but the 45% play rate and 3.9 ALSA suggest it's build-around and often cut; needs real merfolk density to click. Speculative in dedicated UW Merfolk, otherwise a trap. Provisional.
Bitterblossom: Bomb-adjacent faerie engine — the UB Fairies enabler. 57.2% GIH with +8.3 IWD and 1.7 ALSA; the null OH and 52.6% GD hint the life loss makes it awkward in an opening hand but it snowballs the mid-game, flooding evasive tokens exactly as UB wants. Take it very high in Fairies; strong but riskier in slower shells.
Faerie Macabre: Null GIH (6.5% play) — read is provisional. A graveyard-hate faerie whose maindeck body is a below-rate flyer; the format has barely played it, so it's effectively a sideboard card against BG Elves' graveyard-as-resource plan. Don't maindeck unless UB Fairies wants the cheap flash body; otherwise board.
Goblin Chieftain: Strong RB Goblins payoff, near-bomb — but read provisionally, OH/GD WR are null. 56.9% GIH WR and +7.3 IWD confirm a haste-granting lord that snowballs a go-wide board. Take it high if you're in Goblins; it's the kind of tribal payoff whose number is real but deck-dependent.
Goblin Sharpshooter: High-ceiling red rare — 60.7% GIH and +10.8 IWD, and Numot flags it as a near-game-winner that pings on every creature death and untaps, devastating with deathtouch. Null OH_WR from low samples but the drawn WR (61.6%) is real. Take it early in RB Goblins; respect it as a board-controlling engine.
Heat Shimmer: No GIH data (16.8% play, 5.2 ALSA) — read is provisional. A red rare sorcery seeing almost no play suggests a narrow/clone-style effect that doesn't fit the grindy format; low play rate is a soft-negative signal. Treat as a fringe/sideboard card until reps prove otherwise; don't pick it over known playables.
Devoted Druid: Provisional read — oh_wr/gd_wr are null, so lean on the 51.8% GIH and +0.6 IWD, which paint a below-average ramp Elf. A 2/2-ish mana-dork gets blanked in this slow format and ramp is weak here; play it only as a BG Elf-count cog, not for the acceleration.
Helix Pinnacle: Trap — hard pass in Limited. Null WR at 0.2% play rate: a win-con enchantment that's functionally unplayable at this speed and grind. Hate-draft or sideboard curiosity only; there is no ECL deck that assembles 100 mana. Read provisional but the near-zero play rate is damning.
Leaf-Crowned Visionary: Premium green rare, provisional on the null OH_WR. 59.2% GIH, +5.0 IWD, 2.5 ALSA and 84.6% play — an Elf Druid engine that anchors the S-tier BG Elves deck. First-few-picks; the missing opening-hand number doesn't change the verdict given the strong GIH and IWD. Take and commit to Elves.
Regal Force: Provisional / overrated. 51.5% GIH with null OH data and -0.6 IWD says this 70%-played green fatty underperforms its reputation — a big vanilla-ish top-end that loses to the grind without immediate board impact. Playable ramp payoff in Elves, but not the premium the type suggests; take modestly.
Manamorphose: Provisional read (null GIH): the classic free cantrip that fixes mana and replaces itself, best as a Vivid/splash enabler and spell-count filler rather than a card that wins games. The 47.7% play rate at ALSA 4.7 says it's situational. Fine glue for RG/Temur Vivid bases; not a high pick on raw power.
Risen Reef: Near-bomb value engine — 62.2% GIH and +10.1 IWD are elite, an Elemental card-advantage snowball that fuels UR/UG Elementals exactly as the format's resource war demands. Missing OH_WR but 73.7% play confirms it's a slam. First-pick-caliber when you're in elementals.
Slippery Bogle: Null GIH WR — read is provisional. The 11.2% play rate is damning: an evasive hexproof-style body that the field almost never runs, likely because it does too little without auras this set doesn't support well. Treat as filler/sideboard until data proves otherwise. Provisional.
Dolmen Gate: Provisional read — null GIH WR, so lean on evaluation. A 3.2 ALSA and 60.3% play rate suggest drafters value the no-lose-attacker effect, but a defensive artifact with no board presence is a mediocre fit for this grindy, five-toughness format. Treat it as a niche RB/WG go-wide enabler, not a premium pick — provisional.
Door of Destinies: Trap in most seats despite the 84.7% play rate and 2.0 ALSA (people over-draft the shiny rare). 53.6% GIH with +3.7 IWD is only mediocre — a build-around anthem that does nothing the turn it lands and needs a dense single-tribe board to pay off. Take it in committed BG Elves/UW Merfolk; pass otherwise.
Painter's Servant: Trap in Limited — null GIH WR, 19% play rate, ALSA 4.5. It's a mythic with no relevant combo here; a 2/2 that names a color does little for a fair deck and is why people pass it. Provisional read from the sparse data: leave it for Constructed, sideboard at best.
Thousand-Year Elixir: Sideboard/trap artifact — null GIH and a 1.4% play rate mean it's essentially unplayed, and correctly so; a colorless combo piece with no home in ECL Limited. Read is provisional on scarce data but the community verdict is clear: leave it in the pool. Don't maindeck it.
